evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends a seven-to-ten-year interval after complete removal of one or two tubular adenomas under 10 mm at a high-quality examination.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication; average-risk baseline, not a count of pathology fragments or a history of advanced neoplasia.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends three-to-five-year surveillance after three or four small tubular adenomas are completely removed at a high-quality examination.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication; weak recommendation with very-low-quality evidence. Count lesions, not fragments from a shared container.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends three-year surveillance after five to ten tubular adenomas under 10 mm are completely removed at a high-quality examination.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication; not a policy for more than ten adenomas, hereditary disease or a malignant polyp.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Rectal post-treatment MRI response assessment includes T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted evaluation of the treated bed.
evidenceClaims.limitation: A nondiagnostic component cannot supply its missing observation; this does not define a universal artifact-management protocol.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: An abnormal FIT screening result requires diagnostic colonoscopy; repeating stool screening does not complete that evaluation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One federal recommendation. Does not diagnose cancer or rank investigations when colonoscopy is contraindicated.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: A benign fragment from outside a suspicious colonic lesion does not establish that lesion's histology.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Anatomic application of sampling limitations. Repeat sampling can be appropriate; a concerning nonendoscopically removable lesion may warrant oncologic resection despite nondiagnostic biopsy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Cecal intubation does not complete a diagnostic examination when mucosal visualization remains inadequate after cleaning; an adequately prepared repeat is needed.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No universal same-day/next-day deadline, bowel-prep score cutoff or purgative regimen is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: After confident complete removal at a high-quality examination, an adenoma at least 10 mm warrants USMSTF colonoscopic surveillance in three years.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication, average-risk post-polypectomy context; not a malignant-polyp interval.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends the first surveillance colonoscopy about six months after piecemeal resection of an adenoma at least 20 mm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Two related multisociety publications share an evidence base. Do not substitute routine advanced-adenoma timing for the early scar check.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: A completely removed sessile serrated lesion containing dysplasia warrants USMSTF surveillance in three years after a high-quality examination.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication; weak recommendation with very-low-quality evidence. Complete resection and pathology confidence are necessary.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: After an advanced adenoma at baseline and a normal first surveillance colonoscopy, USMSTF recommends the next examination in five years.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication; weak recommendation with low-quality evidence. Prior CRC, hereditary disease, incomplete exams and additional lesions change applicability.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Large nonpedunculated colorectal lesions without deep invasive features should be assessed by an endoscopist experienced in advanced resection before surgery for technical difficulty.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Size at least 20 mm supports advanced expertise; choice among EMR, ESD or surgery depends on detailed lesion assessment. A superficial biopsy does not exclude focal invasion.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Failure to lift after injection can reflect prior biopsy, cautery or tattoo-related fibrosis as well as invasive cancer.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single primary guideline. Nonlifting neither proves cancer nor guarantees safe routine snare resection.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends mechanical stalk ligation before resection for a pedunculated polyp with head at least 20 mm or stalk thickness at least 5 mm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single primary guideline. The new example is well beyond the threshold. No exclusive ranking of clips versus a detachable loop or injection-based alternatives is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends hot-snare resection for pedunculated colorectal lesions at least 10 mm, with specimen retrieval for histology.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single primary guideline. This does not generalize to small nonpedunculated lesions.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: An intact, fully assessed malignant-polyp specimen with favorable grade, superficial submucosal invasion, absent lymphovascular/perineural invasion, low budding and clear margins can support endoscopic treatment with surveillance.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly verified surgical guideline. Its low-risk definition uses submucosal depth under 1 mm. Exact margin definitions remain debated; examples use clear 2-mm margins rather than the disputed close-margin zone.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Lymphovascular invasion, poor differentiation or a positive/indeterminate invasive-polyp margin supports discussion of oncologic segmental resection with regional lymphatic drainage.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Surgical fitness and goals matter. Negative CT nodes and a healed scar do not exclude microscopic regional disease. No individual probability is claimed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Carcinoma confined to the colonic mucosa, completely excised with an intact assessed submucosa, is treated differently from submucosally invasive malignant polyps and can be managed locally.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Complete local excision and tissue adequacy are required. No inference of absent invasion from a superficial biopsy is allowed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: FAP with rectal adenomas that cannot be cleared endoscopically favors proctocolectomy; preserved continence and a restorative goal can support IPAA.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; conditional/low-quality evidence. No automatic polyp-count threshold or procedure ranking independent of function and goals.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis can be considered in FAP with relative rectal sparing and endoscopically removable rectal adenomas, with continuing rectal surveillance.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline. Operation choice is shared; offered alternatives must not treat IRA as mandatory for every patient with few rectal polyps.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Poor sphincter function can favor proctocolectomy with end ileostomy instead of restorative IPAA in FAP requiring rectal removal.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; no invented manometric threshold or absolute contraindication. The patient's informed functional priority remains necessary.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: After IPAA for FAP, annual endoscopy should assess the pouch and any retained rectal or anal-transition-zone mucosa.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline. Does not specify automatic excision of all polyps or end upper-GI surveillance.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Rectal-protocol pelvic MRI evaluates tumor depth, regional nodes and the relationship of disease to the mesorectal fascia for treatment planning.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Diagnostic abdominal/pelvic CT does not supply equivalent local staging. No CRM cutoff is invented.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Endorectal ultrasound can complement MRI when distinguishing early rectal submucosal from muscularis-propria invasion would change local-excision eligibility.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; operator-dependent, complementary rather than a universal replacement for MRI.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Local excision is an option for selected small favorable cT1N0 rectal cancers; it does not remove or stage mesorectal nodes.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Example eligibility follows the guideline: under 3 cm and under 30% circumference, favorable differentiation, no adverse vascular/neural/budding features and transanal accessibility.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Muscularis-propria invasion found after local rectal excision generally warrants radical resection in an operable patient despite a clear local margin.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Completion TME addresses regional disease not treated by scar excision. Organ-preserving alternatives for patients refusing or unfit for surgery require individualized review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Total neoadjuvant therapy is generally recommended for stage II/III mid or low rectal adenocarcinoma; treatment is planned before radical surgery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Selected example has proficient mismatch repair and a threatened local plane; no drug doses, cycle counts, fixed interval or ranking of TNT sequences is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: A tumor entirely above the anterior peritoneal reflection can follow an upper-rectal pathway with initial resection rather than routine neoadjuvant pelvic radiation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; conditional recommendation. T4b disease, threatened posterior fascia or extramural vascular invasion may change the plan. Distance from anal verge is not a fixed anatomic substitute.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Post-neoadjuvant rectal response assessment integrates current examination, endoscopy and rectal MRI rather than mixing pretreatment and post-treatment records.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No fixed optimal assessment date or near-complete-response interval is asserted. Performed but unexported acquisitions should be distinguished from absent studies.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: A clinical complete response requires concordant examination, endoscopic and MRI findings without residual tumor or suspicious nodes; it is not proof of pathological eradication.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No universal binary inference from one modality. Original fictional observations apply the criteria; uncertain near-complete response remains on the owner hold.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: A negative superficial biopsy after rectal neoadjuvant treatment does not exclude deeper residual tumor when examination and MRI remain concerning.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; biopsy evidence is very low quality. New example uses increasing palpable nodularity and diffusion restriction, not a small shrinking equivocal ulcer.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Selected patients with a clinical complete rectal response may choose protocolized watch-and-wait in an experienced program after counseling; persistent tumor calls for oncologic resection assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Surgery remains valid after complete response. No automatic preference-based key or indefinite observation of proven residual disease.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Localized regrowth during watch-and-wait warrants staging and salvage oncologic surgical assessment when resectable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No claim that all regrowth is salvageable or that every patient requires the same operation. Example has biopsy-proven regrowth and completed negative distant staging.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Curative surgery for colon cancer adherent to an adjacent organ should preserve an en-bloc specimen rather than separate the adhesion through the tumor interface.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; actual organ-resection extent depends on anatomic involvement and ability to obtain clear margins. Adhesion alone is not a pathological T4b diagnosis.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: When fewer than 12 nodes are reported after colon cancer resection, additional pathology evaluation of the submitted specimen should be requested before relying on node-negative staging.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; no automatic repeat colectomy or inference that an inadequate count proves nodal metastasis.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: A discontinuous pericolic tumor deposit can establish N1c regional involvement even when retrieved lymph nodes are negative.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One government summary; requires pathologist-confirmed deposit rather than assuming every pericolic nodule is one. No copyrighted staging table is reproduced.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: After complete resection of nonmetastatic colon cancer with regional nodal disease, adjuvant systemic chemotherapy is considered; FOLFOX is an established option.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One government evidence summary. Oncology individualizes regimen and duration; the questions do not choose between FOLFOX and CAPOX or specify a current molecular-treatment policy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: For incurable metastatic colon cancer with an asymptomatic primary, initial systemic treatment is generally preferred over prophylactic colectomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; symptoms, potentially resectable metastases and curative conversion strategies alter the decision. No particular drug regimen is ranked.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Perforated colon cancer requires source control with an oncologic surgical plan; endoluminal stenting is contraindicated in the perforated setting.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One guideline; resuscitation is concurrent background care. Diversion/anastomosis choices remain individualized. Outside-hospital chart review, not emergency care delivered by this clinic.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Bowel-preparation adequacy is judged from mucosal visibility after endoscopist cleansing rather than the uncleaned insertion view.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One official ACG summary of the 2025 USMSTF consensus; assessment-after-cleansing has low-quality support. This summary and its parent recommendation are one publication, not independent corroboration.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: USMSTF recommends repeat screening in ten years after a normal complete high-quality colonoscopy in the applicable average-risk setting.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline. Prior neoplasia, hereditary disease, relevant family history, incomplete examination or inadequate final visibility changes applicability.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: After the first approximately six-month surveillance following piecemeal removal of a lesion at least 20 mm, USMSTF recommends the next surveillance one year after that first examination.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single publication. This is the subsequent visit, not a one-year substitute for the initial scar check. No recurrence-management algorithm is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: For a colon cancer attached to a limited bladder portion, en-bloc partial bladder resection can preserve uninvolved bladder when clear margins and a useful remnant are achievable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: ASCRS supports en-bloc removal; the anatomy-specific bladder-preserving example is cross-checked in one retrospective single-center cohort. It does not establish a universal reservoir cutoff or a survival advantage caused by partial rather than total cystectomy. Neck/trigone involvement and achievable margins may require a different extent.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Regional-node findings must remain assigned to their primary tumor and resection specimen when assessing a separate cancer basin.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Anatomic/provenance application of regional drainage and specimen-based node assessment to constructed synchronous primaries; neither source is represented as an empirical trial of pooling counts. Five plus seventeen is not a clinical rate or new threshold.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: The inability of one colonoscope to pass a tumor does not by itself establish a primary-related complication requiring prophylactic local treatment in otherwise asymptomatic incurable metastatic disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Constructed application of the guideline asymptomatic-primary versus obstructing-primary distinction. No validated obstruction score, guaranteed future patency or numerical dilation cutoff is claimed; symptoms and imaging still require clinical judgment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: After resection of a perforated left-colon cancer, continuing circulatory instability and adverse contamination or tissue conditions favor avoiding primary anastomosis and considering an end colostomy with rectal-stump closure.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Two surgical guidelines; evidence is low quality and reconstruction remains individualized. Scope is the current after-resection decision with feasible closure, not an automatic rule for all perforations, all metastases or patients requiring an open abdomen. No dose or physiologic cutoff is invented.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: CT colonography may help evaluate the proximal colon when a distal colon cancer prevents complete colonoscopy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One society guideline. Used only to ground the counterfactual anatomic completion alternative; it is not promoted as routine replacement for colonoscopy after abnormal FIT with a correctable preparation deficit.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The explicitly scoped fictional colorectal clinic/chart-review decision; not an autonomous patient-care rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Histology of submitted dysplastic fragments describes those fragments, while pelvic MRI assesses represented local extent; neither observation alone establishes the absence of microscopic invasion throughout an unsampled rectal field.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Scope/provenance application of histologic sampling and radiologic local staging, not an accuracy estimate or an absolute limit on all imaging. The new case does not assume MRI determines the histologic status of every adenoma.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The fictional post-IRA rectal-field chart review.

claim.statement: Bleeding, ulceration, clinically significant symptoms, obstruction, or diagnostic uncertainty makes the asymptomatic observation-only lipoma pathway inapplicable and requires further individualized evaluation.

claim.statement: A positive screening FIT requires diagnostic colonoscopy; FIT alone does not diagnose colorectal cancer.
claim.limitation: Suitability and the management of incomplete examination remain individualized.

claim.statement: Histologic examination of tissue sampled from a suspicious colorectal lesion provides confirming evidence of cancer.
claim.limitation: Gross appearance and cross-sectional imaging can be suspicious but do not substitute for tissue diagnosis or assign stage here.
claim.applicablePopulation: Adults with a suspicious colorectal lesion sampled during colonoscopy.

claim.statement: Colonoscopy with inadequate cleansing may fail to assess the colonic lining adequately.
claim.limitation: Official ESGE guideline plus directly read 2025 society summary; the latter is not the full USMSTF guideline. Cases specify inadequate assessment throughout the colon after attempted cleaning, excluding the partial-distal-examination exception.
claim.applicablePopulation: Adults reviewing a colonoscopy that cannot support a standard screening assessment.

claim.statement: An inadequately prepared colonoscopy that cannot support the intended assessment should be repeated with adequate preparation.
claim.limitation: Current society summary corroborates guideline direction. No universal numerical interval or mandatory same/next-day schedule; timing, contraindications and urgency require the treating team's assessment. Alternative screening proposals do not complete the inadequate examination in these cases.
claim.applicablePopulation: Adults suitable for repeat colonoscopy after an entirely inadequate screening examination.

claim.statement: Reviewing why preparation failed can guide improved instructions and an individualized repeat-preparation plan.
claim.limitation: Source-supported planning only. No specific laxative formulation, dose, diet duration, split-dose timetable or contraindication protocol is authored.
claim.applicablePopulation: Adults planning repeat colonoscopy after inadequate bowel cleansing.
